memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage Assessment, medium conviction. Not a park and not an unqualified progression. Conditional on two binary diagnostics: (1) establish whether Q2 2026 sustained the Q1 2026 pattern of absolute volumes and adjusted operating profit per kilo rising together, the single disconfirming test of the false-friend hypothesis; (2) explain the roughly 28% fall from the 52-week high, which post-dates every research report on disk. Direction stated in the memo: constructive, not yet bullish. The case earns further work; it does not yet earn capital. Two memo-level downstream actions: Investment Analyst to open Early-Stage Assessment with a Q1-versus-Q2 2026 volume and unit-margin reconciliation as its first block, on the next memo cycle; Chief of Staff to commission a refreshed developments-family report covering 19-Jun-26 forward, front of queue.
case: The business is the best in its assigned comparison set by a wide margin and is simultaneously the cheapest against its own history. Return on capital employed of 20.9% in FY25 sits against Corbion at 9.9%, Tate & Lyle at 8.2% pro forma, Trelleborg at 12.1% and Syensqo at 6.2%. Adjusted operating profit has not fallen in a full year since 2009, when it fell 3%, and grew in 18 of the 20 years since the 2005 merger. Adjusted operating profit compounded at 14% between 2013 and 2023 against a 10% guided long-term target, and at 18% since 2020.

Both change-force legs fire and are dated. The external force is the cocoa-price-driven shift into AAK's cocoa butter alternatives, quantified in the sources as a 0.41 R-squared between cocoa price changes and confectionery lipid profitability at a one-quarter lag and a negative 0.38 correlation with confectionery volumes at a two-quarter lag. It is material because Chocolate and Confectionery Fats is approximately 40% of group operating profit. It is sticky because reformulated recipes remain highly stable, manufacturers rarely reverting to costly cocoa butter, and because displacing a formulation takes 12 to 24 months of validation plus shelf-life studies of up to two years. The internal force is Fit-to-Win, guided at SEK 300m of annual savings with full run rate by mid-2026, launched early 2025 with a headcount reduction of up to 5% and a SEK 250m restructuring charge in Q2 2025, which delivered just north of SEK 150m in 2025 against a SEK 50m initial expectation.

The base is well invested where recovery would land. Spare production capacity of 15% to 20% allows volume expansion at minimal incremental capital. Completed Denmark biomass boilers cost SEK 500m and generate SEK 100m of annual savings. Over 60 active innovation projects run across sixteen customer innovation centres.
counter_case: The risks report's own recommendation, quoted verbatim in memo Section F.6, is "We recommend a Proceed decision, conditional on the strict quarterly monitoring of customer co-development pipelines and commodity spot prices", and in its fuller form to proceed to the final investment committee stage, conditional on strict quarterly monitoring of volume recovery, customer co-development pipelines and commodity price normalisation. The memo ADOPTS that direction rather than overriding it, records that no evidence in the memo beats the risks report, and adds one condition the risks report could not have carried, because its Proceed was formed at a materially higher share price and pre-dates the price break. It also adopts the risks report's own revisit trigger verbatim as its park trigger: a consecutive two-quarter decline in group absolute volumes.

The dominant counter is the false friend, and it is carried at full force. The risks report's Analysis of Competing Hypotheses names the false-friend profile the winning hypothesis, with only two disconfirming items against three for the no case and seven for the yes case. Its diagnostic is rising adjusted operating profit per kilo alongside declining absolute specialised lipid volumes. That signature is already in the record: operating profit per kilo rose 26% from SEK 1.94 in 2023 to SEK 2.45 in 2025 while reported volumes fell 8% to 2,010,000 metric tonnes. The named mechanism, restructuring savings masking volume decay, is live: Fit-to-Win banked SEK 150m against a SEK 50m guide, which the risks report reads as front-loading rather than sustainable incremental reduction, and management actively targets a SEK 3.00-plus per kilo aspiration. The only disconfirming evidence on file is a single quarter, Q1 2026, where 3% organic volume growth and SEK 2.49 per kilo occurred together.
triggers: - Key question one: did absolute group volumes and adjusted operating profit per kilo rise together in Q2 2026, and if not, which one broke.
- Key question two: did the working-capital build land at the projected SEK 1.1bn, and did it suspend or slow the SEK 3bn buyback.
- Key question three: how much of the FY25 volume decline was deliberate low-margin pruning versus lost business, since the two have opposite implications for the moat.
- Key question four: what is the current cocoa butter to specialty fat spread, which the tearsheet names the single most important swing factor for earnings.
- Key question five: has the sell-side begun cutting estimates materially since the price break, which would move the clearing-event setup from [C] toward [B].

- Trigger to park, one: two consecutive quarters of declining absolute group volumes, the risks report's own single most critical revisit trigger, which would prove pruning had crossed into terminal decay.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
